cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: You Could at Least…
cards.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved this position for my wet sock: beside your dinner. It came through your puddle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you take it away? It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removal is pending. You may explain why only water was worth leaving where I would step.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wipe the floor. Just move the sock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Floor repair is approved. Add 'I'm sorry' and I'll remove the sock. You may finish dinner without looking at what my foot went through.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 withholds removal approval and A5 approves the practical repair only alongside the apology that clears the visible inconvenience.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 water minimization causes A3 demand for explanation; B4 wiping offer causes A5 acceptance plus the simpler apology condition.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants dinner cleared and B4 offers a real repair, making apology a response to displayed inconvenience rather than arbitrary coercion.

heightening.evidence: B4 practical solution is insufficient to end the display until A5 names the brief acknowledgment that will.

specificity.evidence: A1 wet sock beside dinner and puddle origin establish the complaint and visible leverage.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 what-my-foot-went-through refers directly to the wet sock and puddle, replacing the earlier obscure dinner metaphor.
